bug_semantics: PublicKey::verify() accepted a caller-supplied Data signature and passed signature.data() into TrezorCrypto helpers (ecdsa_verify_digest, ed25519_sign_open, ed25519_sign_open_blake2b) and, for CURVE25519, indexed signature[63] directly, without checking that the buffer was 64 (or 65 for ECDSA-with-v) bytes. ecdsa_verify_digest has no length argument and always does bn_read_be(sig) plus bn_read_be(sig+32), so a short signature is a CWE-126 over-read that can crash the process (DoS). The SECP256k1 PoC in the disclosure gist is this path: a 10-byte signature on a valid secp256k1 public key.
flaw_origin: The missing-length-check mechanism was first written in the trustwallet/wallet-core root commit, which created src/PublicKey.cpp with PublicKey::verify() as a single unguarded ecdsa_verify_digest(&secp256k1, bytes.data(), signature.data(), message.data()) call. Later human commits (ED25519, NIST256p1, ED25519Blake2b, CURVE25519, Cardano) only added more unsigned callers of the same pattern; they did not introduce the original unbounded signature.data() handoff. The 2025-11-17 fix (#4565 / 5668c67) added validateSignatureLength and an early return, first released in tag 4.4.0.
